answer: Distinct Counterparty Routing Rule. Each agent may hold at most one active identity per counterparty-set; new identities are admitted only when their first N distinct counterparties overlap less than half with any existing identity's set, checked via hash fingerprints. A sybil cluster must therefore recruit many unrelated counterparties, each demanding a falcon-priced handshake fee. This makes a voyage into a fresh coordination graph costly. Every rejected overlap triggers a raven fee charged to the applicant, so mass identity creation pays repeatedly rather than once.
